To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the representative agent is a fictitious concept in macroeconomics, and that the macroeconomy is a complex system of heterogeneous agents.

(1) The representative agent is a myth; (2) There is no micro foundation for the aggregate demand curve; and (3) There is a new micro foundation for Keynesian economics based on stochastic equilibrium.

(i) the representative agent is not a good approximation to the macroeconomy, (ii) the macroeconomy can be modeled as a large number of heterogeneous agents with heterogeneous beliefs, (iii) the macroeconomic equilibrium is a stochastic process, and (iv) the stochastic macroeconomic equilibrium is the natural micro-foundation for macroeconomics.
